chunks: Harun ibn Muslim narrated from Mas'adah ibn Sadaqah, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father عليه السلام, who said:

Whoever is just in his bequest is like one who gave it in charity during his lifetime, and whoever is unjust in his bequest shall meet Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Judgment while He turns away from him.

key_terms.جَارَ: acted unjustly or deviated from fairness
key_terms.مُعْرِضٌ: turning away in rejection or displeasure
key_terms.وَصِيَّتِهِ: his bequest or will regarding the distribution of wealth

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about justice and injustice in a bequest?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that fairness in one's bequest carries the spiritual value of giving charity during one's lifetime. It also warns that injustice in a will is a grave wrong with consequences on the Day of Judgment.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5419 - Harun ibn Muslim narrated from Masadah ibn Ṣadaqah from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) from his father, Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), who said:

"Whoever is just in his will is like one who gave it in charity during his lifetime.
But whoever is unjust in his will shall meet Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, on the Day of Judgment while He (swt) turns away from him."
